To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents, forms, communications (written or digital), and any other type of record(s) related to the scheduling and actual maintenance outage of the North Truro, Massachusetts, radar site on September 11, 2001, that were collected in part due to the investigation of PENTTBOM. The radar site is designated as a Joint Surveillance System facility J-53 with the FAA and the Air Force.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Charles Kallas

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents, forms, communications (written or digital), and any other type of record(s) related to the scheduling and actual maintenance outage of the North Truro, Massachusetts radar site on September 11, 2001. The radar site is designated as a Joint Surveillance System facility J-53 with the FAA and the Air Force.

According to FAA Form 7230-4, the Daily Record of Facility Operation by Chief Heather Hemdal, dated 9/11/2001, indicates that at 1200 UTC, the North Truro, MA radar was released for maintenance; it can be found at https://catalog.archives.gov/id/7598468 on PDF page 4. 

In a FOIA response, the FAA indicated, "All records pertaining to September 11, 2001 have been transferred to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)," which is why this FOIA is being requested.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Charles Kallas
